Q598.L1t: Radioactive decay is a process in which the amount of an unstable isotope falls over time.
Q598.L2t: Decay of this kind is exponential, so the sample loses the same fraction in every equal time interval, not the same mass.
Q598.L3t: The sample keeps 90% of its mass every 9 days, so the question becomes how many 9-day periods it takes for 0.9 raised to that power to equal 0.4, which is a little under 9 periods.
Q598.L4t: The sample reaches 20 grams about seventy-eight days after the start.
Q598.L2f: Radioactive isotopes lose mass at a steady number of grams per unit time, which is why a sample always reaches zero after a fixed period.
Q598.L3f: The isotope loses a constant 5 grams every 9 days, so losing 30 grams in total takes exactly 6 such periods.
Q598.L4f: The sample will be down to 20 grams after fifty-four days.

Q614.L1t: Angles can be measured in degrees, and a full rotation is a fixed number of degrees.
Q614.L2t: Spinning to the right means turning clockwise, so north turns toward east, then south, then west.
Q614.L3t: A full turn is 360 degrees, so 2250 degrees is six full turns plus a remainder of 90 degrees, and a clockwise quarter turn from north faces the next compass point.
Q614.L4t: After the spin she is facing east.
Q614.L2f: Skaters usually spin counterclockwise because that is the natural direction for most athletes, so a spin to the right is unusual.
Q614.L3f: 2250 degrees is an exact multiple of 360, so she completes whole turns only and ends exactly where she began.
Q614.L4f: After the spin she ends up facing the same direction she started, which is north.

Q793.L1t: The passage compares the lives of children and teens today with those of earlier generations.
Q793.L2t: The author notes that a few decades ago children used to work and that some girls were married at thirteen.
Q793.L3t: The passage begins by saying children would rather play with new technologies, and it describes teens spending their free time texting, calling and using social networking sites, so technology is what has changed their daily lives.
Q793.L4t: Their role has changed mainly because new technologies keep developing and are widely used.
Q793.L2f: The passage says that earlier generations had access to far more gadgets than children and teens have today.
Q793.L3f: The passage gives the general evolution of the world over the years as the underlying cause of the change, and treats technology and work as minor details.
Q793.L4f: The change in children's and teens' roles is mainly because the world itself has evolved through the years.
